title: Energy and Policy Considerations for Deep Learning in NLP
authors: Emma Strubell, Ananya Ganesh, Andrew McCallum
abstract: Recent progress in hardware and methodology for training neural networks has ushered in a new generation of large networks trained on abundant data. These models have obtained notable gains in accuracy across many NLP tasks. However, these accuracy improvements depend on the availability of exceptionally large computational resources that necessitate similarly substantial energy consumption. As a result these models are costly to train and develop, both financially, due to the cost of hardware and electricity or cloud compute time, and environmentally, due to the carbon footprint required to fuel modern tensor processing hardware. In this paper we bring this issue to the attention of NLP researchers by quantifying the approximate financial and environmental costs of training a variety of recently successful neural network models for NLP. Based on these findings, we propose actionable recommendations to reduce costs and improve equity in NLP research and practice.
explain_beginner: This paper examines the hidden costs of modern language AI systems. While these systems have become remarkably good at understanding text, training them requires enormous amounts of electricity and expensive computer hardware. The researchers measured how much energy and money it takes to build popular AI language models, revealing that these expenses create barriers for researchers without access to well-funded labs. They then suggest practical ways to make this technology more accessible and environmentally responsible.
explain_business: Training advanced language AI models demands substantial capital investment in specialized hardware and energy costs, creating competitive advantages for well-resourced organizations. This paper quantifies those expenses and demonstrates how resource constraints limit who can participate in AI development. For businesses, the findings suggest that operational efficiency and cost reduction in model training directly impact competitiveness. The recommendations indicate that optimizing training approaches not only reduces expenses but also expands the potential talent pool by lowering barriers to entry for smaller competitors and academic institutions.
explain_practitioner: The authors quantified the computational, financial, and carbon costs associated with training state-of-the-art neural language models. They measured electricity consumption and hardware expenses across several prominent NLP architectures trained on large datasets. Their analysis demonstrated significant disparities in resource requirements and accessibility. The paper provides specific cost metrics for different model types and training approaches, then offers evidence-based recommendations for practitioners to reduce resource consumption and improve equity in model development and research.
